paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. The LORD made His people to cling to Him like a loincloth clings to a man's waist, "so that they might be My people for My renown and praise and glory" (Jeremiah 13:11). That is how close He wanted them. But they did not listen. They followed "the stubbornness of their own hearts" and went after other gods (Jeremiah 13:10).

So the loincloth is a warning, and it's a serious one. A loincloth that was never meant to leave a man's side ended up ruined, "of no use at all" (Jeremiah 13:7). Pride does that, friend. It tells you that you already know it all, just like the people who answered, "Don't we surely know..." (Jeremiah 13:12). I think a stubborn heart is the most dangerous thing in my whole bakery, and I'm including the oven.

Here's why this matters to you, baker. The LORD didn't hide His words from anyone. He sent them through Jeremiah, plainly, and He wanted a people who would listen. So when you open the Word, come ready to listen, even to the parts you think you already know. Stay close to Him, and keep your ears open.
